title: Options definition
claim: Options are derivative contracts providing right (call) or obligation (put) to trade underlying at specified strike price. Options provide leveraged exposure.
support: Options are derivative contracts providing right (call) or obligation (put) to trade underlying at specified strike price. Options provide leveraged exposure.

title: Implied volatility definition
claim: Implied volatility is market's expectation of future realized volatility, extracted from option prices. IV changes affect option prices independent of underlying moves.
support: Implied volatility is market's expectation of future realized volatility, extracted from option prices. IV changes affect option prices independent of underlying moves.

title: Call option characteristics
claim: Buying call options creates unlimited upside, defined downside (premium paid). Call buyers profit from rising prices and volatility increases.
support: Buying call options creates unlimited upside, defined downside (premium paid). Call buyers profit from rising prices and volatility increases.

title: Put option characteristics
claim: Buying put options creates defined downside (premium paid), unlimited upside on stock decline. Put buyers profit from falling prices.
support: Buying put options creates defined downside (premium paid), unlimited upside on stock decline. Put buyers profit from falling prices.

title: Time value decay
claim: Time value (extrinsic value) decreases as expiration approaches. Theta (time decay) accelerates near expiration, especially out-of-the-money options.
support: Time value (extrinsic value) decreases as expiration approaches. Theta (time decay) accelerates near expiration, especially out-of-the-money options.

title: Call buying fundamentals
claim: Buying calls provides leveraged upside exposure with limited downside risk (limited to premium paid). Call buyers benefit from price appreciation and volatility expansion.
support: Buying calls provides leveraged upside exposure with limited downside risk (limited to premium paid). Call buyers benefit from price appreciation and volatility expansion.

title: Put buying and downside protection
claim: Buying puts provides downside protection or bearish exposure. Put buyers benefit from price declines and implied volatility expansion, with defined maximum loss.
support: Buying puts provides downside protection or bearish exposure. Put buyers benefit from price declines and implied volatility expansion, with defined maximum loss.

title: Vertical spread risk-reward optimization
claim: Vertical spreads (buying and selling options at different strikes) reduce net premium outlay and define maximum profit and loss. Used for income generation with managed risk.
support: Vertical spreads (buying and selling options at different strikes) reduce net premium outlay and define maximum profit and loss. Used for income generation with managed risk.

title: Vertical spread directional biasing
claim: Bull call and bear put spreads provide directional bias with defined risk. Bear call and bull put spreads are used for income in neutral markets.
support: Bull call and bear put spreads provide directional bias with defined risk. Bear call and bull put spreads are used for income in neutral markets.

title: Delta definition and use
claim: Delta measures rate of change of option value relative to underlying price movement. Delta approximates probability of expiration in-the-money. Delta ranges 0-1 for calls, -1-0 for puts.
support: Delta measures rate of change of option value relative to underlying price movement. Delta approximates probability of expiration in-the-money. Delta ranges 0-1 for calls, -1-0 for puts.

title: Delta as hedge ratio
claim: Delta indicates how many shares of stock are equivalent to one option contract. Used to construct delta-neutral positions and measure portfolio risk.
support: Delta indicates how many shares of stock are equivalent to one option contract. Used to construct delta-neutral positions and measure portfolio risk.

title: Gamma risk in short positions
claim: Gamma measures acceleration of delta. Short gamma positions require active management because delta changes accelerate near-the-money, especially at expiration.
support: Gamma measures acceleration of delta. Short gamma positions require active management because delta changes accelerate near-the-money, especially at expiration.

title: Theta decay benefits short sellers
claim: Theta (time decay) erodes extrinsic value. Short sellers profit from theta decay; theta accelerates as expiration approaches and volatility drops.
support: Theta (time decay) erodes extrinsic value. Short sellers profit from theta decay; theta accelerates as expiration approaches and volatility drops.

title: Vega: volatility sensitivity
claim: Vega measures option price sensitivity to implied volatility changes. Long options benefit from volatility increases; short options benefit from volatility decreases.
support: Vega measures option price sensitivity to implied volatility changes. Long options benefit from volatility increases; short options benefit from volatility decreases.

title: Long straddle volatility play
claim: Buying at-the-money straddle (call + put) profits from large price movement in either direction. Maximum loss is premium paid; profit increases with volatility.
support: Buying at-the-money straddle (call + put) profits from large price movement in either direction. Maximum loss is premium paid; profit increases with volatility.

title: Short strangle income generation
claim: Selling out-of-the-money straddle collects premium and profits if underlying stays within strike range. Used for income in range-bound markets.
support: Selling out-of-the-money straddle collects premium and profits if underlying stays within strike range. Used for income in range-bound markets.

title: Butterfly spreads capital efficiency
claim: Butterfly spreads use multiple options at different strikes to define risk within a narrow band. Efficient use of capital with defined risk/reward.
support: Butterfly spreads use multiple options at different strikes to define risk within a narrow band. Efficient use of capital with defined risk/reward.

title: Range-detection tactics
claim: Identify market ranges using support/resistance levels, moving averages, and RSI. Use non-directional strategies in ranging markets.
support: Identify market ranges using support/resistance levels, moving averages, and RSI. Use non-directional strategies in ranging markets.

title: Ratio spreads in ranges
claim: Sell more options than bought to increase premium collection in narrow ranges. Requires careful management at boundaries.
support: Sell more options than bought to increase premium collection in narrow ranges. Requires careful management at boundaries.

title: Adjustment definition
claim: Adjustments modify existing positions to respond to adverse market movement. Adjust by rolling (moving strike/expiration) or widening spreads.
support: Adjustments modify existing positions to respond to adverse market movement. Adjust by rolling (moving strike/expiration) or widening spreads.
mechanism: Position modification for market change response

title: Rolling strategies
claim: Roll positions by closing current and opening new at different strike/expiration. Common adjustments: roll up profitable shorts, roll threatened longs.
support: Roll positions by closing current and opening new at different strike/expiration. Common adjustments: roll up profitable shorts, roll threatened longs.

title: Order execution importance
claim: Execution quality (bid-ask spread, fill latency, slippage) materially affects profitability. Multi-leg orders require coordinated execution.
support: Execution quality (bid-ask spread, fill latency, slippage) materially affects profitability. Multi-leg orders require coordinated execution.

title: Spread order mechanics
claim: Multi-leg spreads should be entered as single order (reduce risk of partial fills). Use market or limit orders depending on liquidity.
support: Multi-leg spreads should be entered as single order (reduce risk of partial fills). Use market or limit orders depending on liquidity.

title: Margin requirements variability
claim: Margin requirements vary by strategy and broker. Spread margin is typically less than naked option margin. Broker-dependent and regime-sensitive.
support: Margin requirements vary by strategy and broker. Spread margin is typically less than naked option margin. Broker-dependent and regime-sensitive.

title: Position sizing with margin
claim: Position size constrained by margin availability and risk tolerance. Use margin efficiency metrics to optimize capital deployment.
support: Position size constrained by margin availability and risk tolerance. Use margin efficiency metrics to optimize capital deployment.

title: Support and resistance
claim: Support and resistance levels guide entry and exit timing. Use price history, moving averages, and pivot points to identify levels.
support: Support and resistance levels guide entry and exit timing. Use price history, moving averages, and pivot points to identify levels.

title: Trend following
claim: Identify trends using moving averages and price patterns. Trade in direction of trend with trend-following indicators.
support: Identify trends using moving averages and price patterns. Trade in direction of trend with trend-following indicators.

title: Earnings-driven volatility
claim: Implied volatility spikes before earnings releases and collapses after. Create opportunities to sell volatility pre-earnings and buy post-earnings.
support: Implied volatility spikes before earnings releases and collapses after. Create opportunities to sell volatility pre-earnings and buy post-earnings.

title: Economic calendar opportunities
claim: Major economic data releases create volatility spikes. Options strategies can capitalize on anticipated and unanticipated reactions.
support: Major economic data releases create volatility spikes. Options strategies can capitalize on anticipated and unanticipated reactions.

title: Low-stress trading philosophy
claim: Focus on defined-risk strategies with fixed maximum loss. Emphasize position sizing, risk management, and consistent execution over aggressive tactics.
support: Focus on defined-risk strategies with fixed maximum loss. Emphasize position sizing, risk management, and consistent execution over aggressive tactics.

title: Process discipline
claim: Consistent adherence to a planned trading process (entry rules, exit rules, position sizing, adjustments) is key to long-term success.
support: Consistent adherence to a planned trading process (entry rules, exit rules, position sizing, adjustments) is key to long-term success.
